description: Itten's 7 color contrasts formalized as computable properties

contrasts.name: Contrast of Hue
contrasts.description: Colors at maximum hue difference. Purest colors at maximum saturation.
contrasts.formal_definition: High ΔHue in HSL (approaching 180° for pairs), S = 1.0, L = 0.5
contrasts.compute: ΔHue = |H1 - H2| mod 360, then min(ΔHue, 360-ΔHue). High if > 120°.
contrasts.maximum_example: Pure red (#FF0000), pure yellow (#FFFF00), pure blue (#0000FF) triad
contrasts.art_notes: The most basic contrast. Primitive visual energy. Use for maximum vibrancy.

contrasts.name: Contrast of Light and Dark
contrasts.description: Contrast between luminance values. White/black is maximum.
contrasts.formal_definition: High ΔLightness. In CIELAB: high ΔL*.
contrasts.compute: ΔL = |L1 - L2| in HSL or L* in CIELAB. Maximum = black vs white.
contrasts.art_notes: The most powerful spatial contrast. Defines legibility and depth.

contrasts.name: Contrast of Cold and Warm
contrasts.description: Blues/greens (cold) vs oranges/reds (warm). Strongest: blue-orange pair.
contrasts.art_notes: Creates spatial depth — warm advances, cool recedes. Psychedelic art abuse of this creates vibration.

contrasts.name: Complementary Contrast
contrasts.description: Colors opposite on the wheel. At equal saturation, maximum visual vibration.
contrasts.vibration_threshold: Both colors at S > 0.8, L ≈ 0.5 — will vibrate at small sizes
contrasts.art_notes: Adjacent complementary patches vibrate, creating optical illusions. Exploit heavily in moiré context.

contrasts.name: Simultaneous Contrast
contrasts.description: A color appears to change based on its surrounding color. Not a fixed property — an interaction effect.
contrasts.formal_definition: Perceived color of C shifts toward the complement of the surrounding color S_color.
contrasts.example: Gray on orange background looks bluish. Same gray on blue looks orangeish.
contrasts.compute: Not a static property — requires context. Related to lateral inhibition in the visual system.
contrasts.art_notes: THE most important effect for generative art. Your background is never neutral.

contrasts.name: Contrast of Saturation
contrasts.description: Pure saturated color vs. muted/grayed color.
contrasts.formal_definition: High ΔSaturation. One color S = 1.0, other S < 0.3.
contrasts.art_notes: A single saturated color against a field of desaturated colors screams. Used in Expressionism. Use for focal points.

contrasts.name: Contrast of Extension (Quantity)
contrasts.description: The relationship between the area of a color and its visual weight. Itten's 'harmony proportions'.
contrasts.formal_definition: To achieve optical balance, area ratios should be inverse to luminance values.

itten_proportions.note: Yellow is 3x brighter than violet, so needs 1/3 the area to feel balanced

contrasts.art_notes: Breaking these proportions is how you create tension and imbalance intentionally. Very useful for psychedelic overload aesthetics.
